newsitem.title: USA: Lufthansa Cargo ups Cologne-NYK capacity.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo ups Cologne-NYK capacity.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo said it will double capacity on the New York-Cologne run as part of its winter schedule which begins Sunday, October 27.

By substituting five weekly Boeing 747 freighter runs for six DC-8F flights, the airline will add 260 tons per week of freight capacity. Lufthansa Cargo is selling its five DC-8 freighters. The DC-8s had about 40 tons of cargo capacity, while a 747 carriers over 100 tons.
Lufthansa said it will keep New York-Frankfurt freighter service at its current level of six 747 frequencies a week.

In all, the airline is scheduling 34 freighter flights a week to Germany from eight U.S. cities besides New York: Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Fairbanks (Alaska), Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco and Seattle.

The airline also plans to route three ex-Frankfurt freighter flights weekly through Montreal's Mirabel International Airport, giving shippers main-deck capacity westbound between Europe and Central Canada.

Eastbound, from Canada to Europe, Lufthansa's ex-Montreal freight will continue to be trucked to Toronto and flown out on the carrier's daily passenger flights, which include four weekly 747 combi frequencies.
